WMT.rationale: Walmart is a structurally sound, wide-moat retailer with dominant U.S. grocery share (~21%), strong omnichannel execution (8 consecutive quarters of 20%+ eCommerce growth), and a rapidly scaling high-margin platform layer (advertising +46% YoY to ~$6.4B, membership +15%). However, the stock trades at a rich 40.7x P/E (vs. 33x a year ago), leaving limited margin for error. Q1 FY27 results showed solid YoY growth (revenue +7.3%, EPS +19.6%) but QoQ deceleration (EPS -13%, operating cash flow -48%) and management issued cautious guidance amid fuel cost headwinds ($175M hit) and consumer stress warnings. The stock has already corrected ~12% from its May highs, partially re-rating the valuation, but at 40x+ it remains expensive for a ~4% operating margin business. No clear near-term fundamental catalyst exists to drive a re-rating; the next catalyst would be Q2 earnings where guidance could be raised if fuel costs moderate. Net: good business, fair-to-slightly-rich valuation, limited near-term catalyst.
